text:
President Bola Tinubu has said eligible Nigerians can access mortgage loans of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent under the Federal Government’s ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF).
Tinubu, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Tuesday, said the initiative was designed to expand access to affordable, long-term housing finance and help more Nigerians become homeowners.
He explained that beneficiaries could repay the loans over a period of up to 20 years, with an initial deposit of 10 per cent.
Illustrating the arrangement, the President said a Nigerian seeking to purchase a house worth ₦10 million would need an initial deposit of ₦1 million and could repay approximately ₦85,400 monthly over 20 years.
According to him, more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have so far accessed ₦160 billion in mortgages through MREIF.
Tinubu said the Federal Government had also strengthened the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN), through which eligible Nigerians could access housing loans of up to ₦50 million at six per cent interest, with repayment periods of up to 30 years.
He added that contributors to pension schemes could qualify to use up to 25 per cent of their retirement savings towards the initial deposit, while married applicants could submit joint applications with their spouses to improve their chances of accessing higher loan amounts.
The President also highlighted the role of the Family Homes Fund in providing affordable housing for Nigerians who cannot afford mortgage arrangements.
He said the fund had delivered more than 53 social homes for vulnerable and underserved households.
Tinubu further disclosed that the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme was targeting 77,400 affordable homes across the country.
According to him, 100 free homes had been delivered to widows in Kaduna, while another 50 were provided to wives of fallen military personnel in Ibadan.
He added that more than 15,000 housing units were under construction nationwide through the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme.
The President stressed that access to the housing initiatives should be based on eligibility rather than political connections or religious affiliation.
“You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities,” he said.
Tinubu maintained that the programmes were open to Nigerians who met the stipulated requirements, irrespective of their location or beliefs.
He said providing opportunities for hardworking Nigerians to own homes and secure their families’ future remained an important objective of his administration’s economic reforms.
